clauses.reason: Sole operative clause: the order exempts Joseph Tombrink from compulsory retirement for age "for a period of one year ending December 31, 1942". This is the order's own stated expiry, not a report deadline and not an amendment. The end is recorded inclusive as 1942-12-31 (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, under which the exemption ends when 1942-12-31 begins, is the alternative. On the inclusive reading the first day without the exemption is 1943-01-01. Actor: the order itself (President Franklin D. Roosevelt). Mechanism: expiry of the order's own fixed term. No later event amends or extends this order in the held record.

research_rationale:
The held text of EO 9003 (registered working text: American Presidency Project mirror transcription, not an official edition; original not yet held) is a short order dated 1941-12-30. Its only operative sentence exempts Joseph Tombrink from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, for a period of one year, ending 1942-12-31. The order states its own term and contains no renewal, conditional, revocation or successor provision, so the exemption ends on its own terms. Evidence: the stated term "for a period of one year ending December 31, 1942" is the first end. Recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of 1942-12-31); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when 1942-12-31 begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on until-dates). Provisional text under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on transcriptions: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved.
